text: Super Typhoon $\textbf{Haiyan}$ (Yolanda), one of the strongest tropical cyclones ever recorded, devastated the city of $\textbf{Tacloban}$ in the $\textbf{Philippines}$ in November 2013.
explanation: The storm caused massive storm surges and highlighted the vulnerability of the archipelago to extreme weather.

text: In July 2013, $\textbf{Croatia}$ became the 28th member state of the $\textbf{European Union}$, expanding the bloc's borders in the $\textbf{Balkans}$.
explanation: It was the first expansion of the EU since Bulgaria and Romania joined in 2007.

text: The $\textbf{Marmaray}$ rail tunnel opened in 2013, connecting the European and Asian sides of $\textbf{Istanbul}$ under the $\textbf{Bosphorus Strait}$.
explanation: This engineering marvel was the first standard-gauge rail connection between the two continents.

text: A massive meteor exploded over the $\textbf{Chelyabinsk}$ region of $\textbf{Russia}$ in 2013, near the $\textbf{Ural Mountains}$.
explanation: The shockwave injured over 1,000 people and damaged thousands of buildings.

text: In 2013, carbon dioxide levels at the $\textbf{Mauna Loa Observatory}$ in $\textbf{Hawaii}$ surpassed $\textbf{400 ppm}$ for the first time in human history.
explanation: This milestone symbolized the growing impact of human activity on the atmosphere.

text: The $\textbf{One World Trade Center}$ in $\textbf{New York City}$ was completed in 2013, becoming the tallest building in the $\textbf{Western Hemisphere}$.
explanation: It stands at a symbolic height of 1,776 feet.

text: A temporary island named $\textbf{Zalzala Koh}$ emerged off the coast of $\textbf{Gwadar}$, $\textbf{Pakistan}$, following a powerful earthquake in the province of $\textbf{Balochistan}$.
explanation: The mud volcano island appeared in the Arabian Sea but has since eroded away.

text: The $\textbf{Rana Plaza}$ collapse, a disaster highlighting dangerous working conditions in the garment industry, occurred in $\textbf{Dhaka}$, the capital of $\textbf{Bangladesh}$.
explanation: It is considered the deadliest structural failure accident in modern human history.

text: Civil war erupted in $\textbf{South Sudan}$, the world's youngest nation, in late 2013, involving conflict between the Dinka and Nuer ethnic groups.
explanation: The country had only gained independence from Sudan two years prior, in 2011.

text: French forces launched $\textbf{Operation Serval}$ in 2013 to push back Islamist militants in northern $\textbf{Mali}$, a country in the $\textbf{Sahel}$ region.
explanation: The conflict centered around cities like Timbuktu and Gao.

text: The $\textbf{Costa Concordia}$ cruise ship was successfully refloated (parbuckled) off the island of $\textbf{Giglio}$ in $\textbf{Italy}$ in 2013.
explanation: The salvage operation was one of the largest and most expensive in maritime history.

text: In 2013, Russian scientists successfully drilled into $\textbf{Lake Vostok}$, a massive subglacial lake buried beneath the ice of $\textbf{Antarctica}$.
explanation: The lake had been isolated from the outside world for millions of years.

text: The $\textbf{Senkaku Islands}$ (known as Diaoyu in China) were a flashpoint for tensions between $\textbf{Japan}$ and China in the $\textbf{East China Sea}$.
explanation: Japan administers the islands, but both China and Taiwan claim them.

text: The $\textbf{Moore}$ tornado, an EF5 storm, devastated suburbs of Oklahoma City, located in the region known as $\textbf{Tornado Alley}$.
explanation: The tornado caused significant loss of life and destruction of schools.

text: Pope Francis was elected in 2013, becoming the first pope from the $\textbf{Americas}$ and hailing from $\textbf{Argentina}$.
explanation: His election shifted the center of gravity of the Catholic Church away from Europe.

text: The $\textbf{Nicaragua Canal}$ project was approved in 2013, intending to connect the $\textbf{Caribbean Sea}$ and the $\textbf{Pacific Ocean}$ through Lake Nicaragua.
explanation: The project was intended to rival the Panama Canal but faced significant environmental and financial hurdles.

text: The $\textbf{Euromaidan}$ protests began in late 2013 in Independence Square in $\textbf{Kyiv}$, the capital of $\textbf{Ukraine}$.
explanation: The protests were sparked by the government's decision to suspend an association agreement with the European Union.

text: Mount $\textbf{Sinabung}$, a volcano in northern $\textbf{Sumatra}$, Indonesia, erupted in 2013 after being dormant for centuries, displacing thousands.
explanation: Indonesia sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire and has more active volcanoes than any other country.

text: The $\textbf{Westgate}$ shopping mall attack occurred in $\textbf{Nairobi}$, the capital city of $\textbf{Kenya}$.
explanation: The attack was carried out by Al-Shabaab, a militant group based in neighboring Somalia.

text: The $\textbf{ALMA}$ observatory, the world's most powerful radio telescope, was inaugurated in the $\textbf{Atacama Desert}$ of $\textbf{Chile}$.
explanation: The high altitude and extreme dryness of the Atacama make it ideal for astronomy.

text: Severe flooding struck $\textbf{Central Europe}$ in 2013, causing the $\textbf{Danube}$ and $\textbf{Elbe}$ rivers to burst their banks.
explanation: Countries like Germany, Austria, and Hungary were heavily affected by the high water levels.

text: The $\textbf{Salar de Uyuni}$ in $\textbf{Bolivia}$ contains the world's largest lithium reserves, a resource that gained strategic importance in 2013 for battery production.
explanation: It is also the world's largest salt flat, located in the Andes.

text: The $\textbf{Gezi Park}$ protests began in $\textbf{Taksim Square}$ in $\textbf{Istanbul}$, Turkey, initially over urban development plans.
explanation: The protests quickly grew into a wider demonstration of civil unrest across the country.

text: The city of $\textbf{Detroit}$ in $\textbf{Michigan}$ filed for the largest municipal bankruptcy in U.S. history in 2013, highlighting the decline of the $\textbf{Rust Belt}$.
explanation: Detroit was once the heart of the global automobile industry.

text: The $\textbf{Zaatari}$ refugee camp in $\textbf{Jordan}$ became one of the world's largest 'cities' in 2013 due to the influx of refugees from the civil war in $\textbf{Syria}$.
explanation: The camp is located in the desert near the Syrian border.

text: A severe $\textbf{Haze}$ crisis affected $\textbf{Southeast Asia}$ in 2013, caused by illegal slash-and-burn land clearing in $\textbf{Indonesia}$.
explanation: The smoke blanketed Singapore and Malaysia, causing record-breaking pollution levels.

text: The $\textbf{Spratly Islands}$ in the $\textbf{South China Sea}$ saw the beginning of massive land reclamation and artificial island building by $\textbf{China}$.
explanation: This marked a significant escalation in the territorial disputes involving Vietnam, Philippines, and others.

text: The $\textbf{Okhotsk Sea}$ in the Russian Far East was the site of a massive, deep earthquake in 2013 that was felt as far away as $\textbf{Moscow}$.
explanation: It lies between the Kamchatka Peninsula and the Russian mainland.

text: The $\textbf{Ngorongoro Conservation Area}$ is a protected area and World Heritage Site located in $\textbf{Tanzania}$, west of Arusha.
explanation: It is famous for its large volcanic caldera and high density of wildlife.

text: The $\textbf{Strait of Gibraltar}$ experienced border delays in 2013 due to a diplomatic row between $\textbf{Spain}$ and the $\textbf{United Kingdom}$ over an artificial reef.
explanation: Gibraltar is a British Overseas Territory located on the southern tip of the Iberian Peninsula.

text: The $\textbf{Xayaburi Dam}$, the first dam on the lower mainstream of the $\textbf{Mekong River}$, faced criticism in 2013 for its potential impact on fish in $\textbf{Laos}$.
explanation: The Mekong is a vital waterway for millions of people in Southeast Asia.

text: The $\textbf{Curiosity Rover}$ drilled into a rock on Mars in 2013 at $\textbf{Gale Crater}$ to analyze the planet's past habitability.
explanation: The rover found evidence that ancient Mars could have supported microbial life.

text: The $\textbf{Amazon Basin}$ spans nine nations, but the majority of the rainforest (about 60%) is contained within $\textbf{Brazil}$.
explanation: Deforestation rates in the Brazilian Amazon are a critical global environmental indicator.

text: The $\textbf{Pamir Highway}$ is a scenic road traversing the $\textbf{Pamir Mountains}$ through Afghanistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, and $\textbf{Kyrgyzstan}$.
explanation: It is the second-highest international highway in the world.

text: The $\textbf{Suez Canal}$ connects the Mediterranean Sea to the $\textbf{Red Sea}$, separating the African continent from $\textbf{Asia}$ (Sinai Peninsula).
explanation: The canal offers a shorter journey between the North Atlantic and northern Indian Oceans.

text: The $\textbf{Aral Sea}$ in Central Asia continued to shrink in 2013, with the eastern basin of the South Aral Sea drying up completely for the first time.
explanation: This was largely due to water diversion from the Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers for cotton irrigation.

text: The $\textbf{Kuril Islands}$ are a chain of volcanic islands disputed between $\textbf{Russia}$ and $\textbf{Japan}$ since the end of World War II.
explanation: The dispute has prevented the two nations from signing a formal peace treaty.

text: The $\textbf{Strait of Malacca}$ is a narrow stretch of water between the Malay Peninsula and the Indonesian island of $\textbf{Sumatra}$.
explanation: It is one of the most important shipping lanes in the world.

text: The $\textbf{Great Barrier Reef}$ faced threats from port expansion and dredging at Abbot Point in $\textbf{Queensland}$, Australia, in 2013.
explanation: The reef is a UNESCO World Heritage site and sensitive to water quality changes.

text: The $\textbf{Sochi}$ region, located on the coast of the $\textbf{Black Sea}$, underwent massive construction in 2013 in preparation for the 2014 Winter Olympics.
explanation: It is one of the few places in Russia with a humid subtropical climate.
